title: FIU marks 25th season by recalling first Sun Belt Conference football title
text:
FIU marks 25th season by recalling first Sun Belt Conference football title
Florida International University is celebrating its 25th football season in 2026 by revisiting key moments in the program's history, including its first Sun Belt Conference championship on Nov. 27, 2010. On that day at FIU Stadium, the Panthers defeated Arkansas State, 31-24, securing both their inaugural bowl eligibility and a share of the conference title.
The 2010 season saw FIU enter the game with a 5-5 overall record but strong performance in conference play at 5-1. With bowl eligibility and a championship on the line, head coach Mario Cristobal led his team into what would become one of the most significant games in program history. The Panthers had built momentum with five wins out of their previous six games and were averaging high offensive output leading up to the matchup.
During the game, FIU overcame an early deficit thanks to two touchdowns from Darriet Parry. At halftime, Arkansas State tied it up at 17-all. In a back-and-forth second half featuring field goals from Jack Griffin and another touchdown by Arkansas State, FIU found itself trailing late in the fourth quarter. Quarterback Wesley Carroll kept hopes alive with a critical fourth-down completion to T.Y. Hilton near midfield before Hilton scored a decisive go-ahead touchdown on a short slant pass with less than two minutes remaining. Wayne Times added a two-point conversion for insurance points, as Jarvis Wilson later sealed victory for FIU by deflecting Arkansas State’s final pass attempt.
The win marked not only bowl eligibility but also secured at least part of FIU’s first Sun Belt Conference title—a milestone achieved just eight years after launching its football program in 2002 under Cristobal’s leadership.
Looking ahead to its official anniversary season in 2026—now under head coach Willie Simmons—FIU notes it has qualified for six bowl games since inception and produced notable NFL players such as T.Y. Hilton and Jonnu Smith. The school plans ongoing celebrations throughout this landmark year highlighting past achievements and contributors who have shaped Panther football over two-and-a-half decades.
Fans are encouraged to follow along through social media channels dedicated to both FIU Football and general athletics for updates about events commemorating this milestone.
